item.title: [New] Microsoft adds 30 Office CVEs it left out of October Patch Tuesday, three of them Critical, and ships the Office for Mac fixes
item.description:
Vulnerability scanners and patch dashboards keyed on the 13 October CVE list did not know these 30 CVEs; a Critical Word or Outlook RCE that a report shows as absent is one nobody verifies. Macs with Office need their own update.

M365 Apps · Refresh your scanner's CVE feed and confirm Defender Vulnerability Management shows CVE-2026-108439, -108440 and -108448 as remediated on Windows Office builds from October; push the Office for Mac October update through your Mac management channel.

item.title: [New] Two identity-library CVEs published on 15 October: Microsoft Identity Web elevation of privilege and MSAL for Node.js information disclosure
item.description:

Entra · Ask application owners which web APIs use Microsoft.Identity.Web and which Node.js services use @azure/msal-node, and get the fixed package versions from the two MSRC pages into their next release.

item.title: [New] Enterprise app 'Activation status' is now documented: Deactivated can mean tenant sign-in off, the app registration deactivated, or Microsoft disabling the app
item.description:
During a consent-phishing response the label 'Deactivated' is ambiguous: an analyst who sees it may assume Microsoft has already disabled the app, or may re-enable sign-in and believe the app works again. Only the three properties tell which condition applies.

Entra · Update the consent-phishing playbook to read accountEnabled, isDisabled and disabledByMicrosoftStatus through Graph instead of trusting the portal label, and alert when disabledByMicrosoftStatus is set on any service principal in your tenant.

item.title: [New] ID Protection's atypical travel detection is now documented as real-time, not offline, and the 14-day learning period is gone from the page

Entra · Review sign-in-risk Conditional Access policies with this in mind, tell the service desk that travelling users may be challenged at sign-in, and trend unlikelyTravel by DetectionTimingType to see when your tenant moves (query in Hunting).

item.description:

Microsoft has published no documentation for any of the three families.

item.title: [New] Agent ID lifecycle policies (preview): Lifecycle Workflows can disable or delete agent identities that are inactive, have too few sponsors or were not reconfirmed
item.description:
This is the first Microsoft control that removes an agent identity nobody answers for, which is the population incident responders keep finding with standing access. It is also a new way for an identity to be disabled or deleted without an administrator doing it by hand: a production agent whose sponsor ignores a notification stops working, and the actor in the audit trail is the lifecycle service. item.title: [New] Skills in Copilot Chat: users can create, upload and share instruction packages with files or scripts; administrators deploy, block and inventory them in the admin center
item.description:
A skill is instructions plus optional scripts that Copilot invokes on its own when it judges a request relevant, and users can share them with each other and install ones published outside the organization. That is a new path for instructions the tenant did not write to shape what Copilot does with a user's data, and the control point is the Tools registry in the admin center rather than any existing app-consent process.

item.title: [New] Pre-authenticated (tempauth) file URLs retire on 1 April 2027: Graph file APIs stop returning URLs with an embedded token, and a tenant control lets you test per application first
item.description:
A tempauth URL is a bearer credential in a link: whoever holds the URL reads the file with no further authentication for as long as it lives, and it travels through logs, proxies and tickets. Its retirement removes that exposure, and it also breaks every backup tool, migration tool, scanner and line-of-business script that stores, inspects or redeems such URLs or follows the 302 redirect. Applications that call SharePoint URLs directly afterwards need an Entra ID access token for the SharePoint resource, which also means their file access appears in sign-in logs where it did not before.

SharePoint · Ask the owners of backup, DLP, eDiscovery, migration and custom integrations whether they use Graph download, upload-session, copy, preview, thumbnail or version URLs; when the tenant control ships, opt a small set of application IDs in and watch for authentication failures before widening it. Record the vendors' support dates well before April 2027.
